reference.unit: public names imported or lazy-imported by sage.plot.plot3d.all

metric.meaning: Every public top-level SageMath 3D plotting name is callable in Sage.js. This measures symbol presence, not complete option, renderer, or algorithm parity.

facets.name: Public top-level API
facets.detail: 24 of 24 SageMath 10.10.beta7 public plot3d exports are callable.

facets.name: Plots and geometric primitives
facets.detail: Surface, parametric, implicit, list, revolution, vector-field, curve, mesh, text, arrow, sphere, and regular-solid families have focused regressions.

facets.name: Composition and transforms
facets.detail: Scene addition, indexing, translation, scaling, rotation, coordinate transforms, frames, rulers, axes, labels, and aspect-ratio handling are regression tested.

facets.name: Jupyter rendering
facets.detail: Plotly MIME output is self-contained and covered by rich-display and serialization tests.

facets.name: Sampling and interpolation parity
facets.detail: Rectangular and scattered sampling are useful today; Sage adaptive plot3d refinement and some list_plot3d interpolation modes remain missing.

facets.name: Renderer and export parity
facets.detail: Plotly is the supported renderer; Sage Tachyon/Jmol/Three.js renderer selection and the full static export matrix are not reproduced.

facets.name: Materials, textures, and lighting
facets.detail: Colors, opacity, mesh styling, and common scene options work; advanced textures, lighting, and material semantics remain incomplete.

limitations: A callable constructor can still have unsupported specialized keyword options.
Visual equivalence needs image- or scene-level regression tests in addition to object-structure tests.
This audit intentionally does not count Sage internal renderer classes as user-facing top-level plotting API.
